meaning: A managed job queue for container jobs. It starts EC2 instances for a job, places the container on a GPU, retries the job if its instance is lost and removes the instances when the queue is empty.
The AWS service that rents virtual machines, which are called instances.
The AWS service that starts containers on instances. Each Batch compute environment contains an ECS cluster, and its instances join that cluster.
The AWS registry that stores container images. A Batch job pulls its image from it while the job is in the STARTING state.
Managed Kubernetes on AWS. Batch can run its jobs as pods on nodes that it launches into an EKS cluster.
A shared network file system on AWS. A Batch job can mount it as a volume, for example to keep its checkpoints.
Your private network on AWS. Batch launches its instances in the subnets of your VPC.
One hardware thread of an instance. Batch sizes its compute environments in vCPUs, also when they hold GPU instances.
The template of a Batch job. It names the image and the command, and it sets the resources, the retry strategy and the timeout.
The stage a Batch job has reached: SUBMITTED, PENDING, RUNNABLE, STARTING and RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED or FAILED.
The state of a job that is ready and waits for capacity, including the whole time an instance launches for it. A job can stay in this state indefinitely when no capacity is available.
The state of a job that Batch has placed on an instance while its container image is pulled. This time does not count toward the timeout.
One submission that creates 2 to 10,000 child jobs from the same job definition. Each child gets its own index.
One Batch job that spans several instances. Its main node starts first, and the job runs on On-Demand Instances only.
The Batch object where jobs wait. It has a priority and an ordered list of up to three compute environments.
The default order of a Batch queue. The job at the front goes next, and if Batch cannot place it, it blocks the jobs behind it.
A queue policy under which the scheduler takes the next job from the share with the least recent vCPU usage, scaled by a weight. A share is the set of jobs with the same share identifier.
A label on a job that says whose work it is. Fair-share scheduling uses it to divide the capacity.
The pool of capacity behind a Batch queue. It has a type, a list of instance types, an allocation strategy, and a floor and a ceiling in vCPUs.
The three numbers that size a compute environment: the floor it keeps running, the current target that Batch moves with queue demand, and the ceiling.
The rule that Batch follows to choose an instance type from the list when its first choice is not available.
What a compute environment does when its floor, minvCpus, is 0 vCPUs: it holds no instance while its queue is empty.
The time, set with minScaleDownDelayMinutes, that Batch keeps an instance after its last job, so that the next job skips the instance launch.
Spare EC2 capacity that AWS can reclaim after a two-minute warning.
EC2 capacity billed by the second with no commitment. AWS does not reclaim it.
The warning that EC2 sends, on a best-effort basis, two minutes before it reclaims a Spot Instance.
The state that Batch puts an instance in when the Spot notice arrives. Running jobs continue, and Batch places no new job on the instance.
Progress that a job saves to storage that outlives the instance, so that a later attempt can resume instead of starting over.
The part of a job definition that sets how many attempts a job gets and which failures are retried, for example only a status reason that matches Host EC2*.
The Unix signals that ask a process to stop and that force it to stop. When a job times out, Batch sends them 30 seconds apart.
A scheduler stopping a running job to give its capacity to another job. Batch does this only for queues of SageMaker Training jobs.
A reservation of GPU instances for a fixed window, bought in advance.
The AWS event bus. A rule on it can submit a Batch job or react when a job changes state.
A Kubernetes mark on a node that keeps pods off the node unless they tolerate it. Batch taints the EKS nodes it manages.
The Batch object that puts a Batch queue in front of training jobs that Amazon SageMaker runs.
The scheduler that high-performance computing clusters commonly use. AWS offers it through AWS Parallel Computing Service.
One attempt by the policy at the task, from the start to success or failure.
The 500 simulated episodes that test each new policy before it may drive the real arm. Batch runs them as one array job.
A virtual queue nested inside a Batch queue for SageMaker Training jobs. A queue can have up to 20, and they can lend idle capacity to each other and take it back.

An open-source AWS solution that you deploy in your own account. It stores robot models, scenes, datasets and other files in Amazon S3 as versioned assets, and it runs GPU pipelines on them as AWS Batch jobs.
The AWS framework that defines cloud resources in code and deploys them. VAMS is deployed with it.
